You might still be interested in gruits, beers made with herbs other than hops. Gruit is an older style, with as much variation as you see in modern beers. It was outlawed in Germany in 1516, after use of dangerous narcotic herbs like henbane became common. The "Reinheitsgebot", or German Beer Purity Law stated beer must only be brewed with water, hops and barley. A provision for yeast was made later.

With the deregulation of home-brewing in 1980, interest in gruits was renewed. Hops have strong preservative qualities, allowing for long periods of time between bottling and opening. Gruits in contrast must be enjoyed shortly after brewing. Depending on what herbs are used, gruits can have even more nutritious qualities than beer.
